Subject: Initial ask: indemnity carve and evidence SLA

We attached our standard security exceptions doc for context (CH_Special_Security_Reqs.pdf). Can we get a proposal on language that our legal team can review? We have target signature week of Dec 10.

Subject: RE: Initial ask: indemnity carve and evidence SLA

Team — drafting two options below and attaching a tracked Word with proposed redlines (redlines_v1.docx). Short summary: both options limit Redwood's IP indemnity to third-party claims arising from the service or model outputs (not Customer inputs or Customer fine-tuning artifacts), and both include a proactive evidence notice timeline.

Option A (preferred operational compromise):
- Narrowed scope: "Redwood shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Customer from any third-party claim to the extent such claim arises directly from the unmodified, shipped model outputs generated by Redwood's service, and not from Customer-provided data, prompts, or fine-tuned model artifacts created by the Customer."
- Evidence SLA: Customer must provide requested logs, model inputs, and cooperation within 14 calendar days of Redwood's written request; Redwood will preserve relevant runtime logs for 60 days following notice and will provide a signed forensic snapshot on request.
- Insurance/Cap: No change to base cap in MSA; Redwood will offer to extend evidence preservation to 90 days for customers who take our Dedicated plan (commercial upsell).

Option B (negotiation-friendly, includes insurance concession):
- Same narrowed scope language as Option A.
- Evidence SLA shortened to 10 business days for critical claims; Redwood to use commercially reasonable efforts to preserve logs for 90 days.
- Insurance cap: Redwood will agree to add a mutual insurance fallback where each party maintains at least $5M for third-party IP claims (subject to procurement verification).

Notes/risks: both options keep "defend and control" language but require a clear evidence window to avoid stale-data disputes. If ClearHealth insists on a blanket indemnity for all customer outputs, we should push to an escrow/insurance offset instead.

I'll attach redlines_v1.docx (tracked) with the proposed text for the MSA and Order Form.

Kimberly Park
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference

Kimberly — thanks for the rapid options and the tracked redlines. Option A is close to what our GC will accept but we need clarity on two points before we can proceed to DocuSign: 1) Defend vs. Reimburse: we prefer "defend" with Redwood controlling counsel and invoicing for third-party costs limited to pre-approved counsel. Can Redwood accept language that allows Customer input on counsel selection when there is a material conflict? 2) Evidence preservation: ClearHealth's compliance team requires a binding commitment that logs supporting the claim will be retained for 90 days unless both parties agree to a shorter term.

We're prepared to sign quickly if those two items are addressed. I've attached the CH security exceptions for your legal review again.

Alex

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RE: RE: Initial ask: indemnity carve and evidence SLA

Alex — appreciate the quick read. Kimberly and I discussed and propose the following concrete compromise to move to signature by Dec 10:

- Defend vs Reimburse: Redwood will "defend" and control the defense with Redwood-appointed counsel; Customer may reasonably object to counsel on conflict grounds and, if a conflict exists, counsel acceptable to both parties will be appointed. Redwood will not invoice Customer for Redwood's defense costs.

- Evidence preservation: Redwood will commit to preserving relevant runtime logs and snapshots for 90 days from written notice of a claim for customers on the Hosted plan; for Dedicated customers Redwood will preserve logs for 180 days. Customer will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide required inputs/evidence within 14 calendar days of Redwood's request; failure to provide timely evidence may be considered in any indemnity determination.

- MSA wording: adopt Option A narrowed scope language (see Kimberly's redlines_v1.docx) with an added sentence clarifying that indemnity does not apply to claims arising from Customer modifications, fine-tuning, or third-party model components provided by Customer.

Ben/Laura — can you confirm commercial OK to add the tiered evidence preservation (Hosted 90d / Dedicated 180d) and that we can include this as an order form checkbox (Dedicated = extended preservation)? If yes, I'll share the tracked language with Alex and ask ClearHealth to confirm by EOD Wed so we can circulate to procurement and legal.

—Sergio
